answer: The Hardware security key bound by DNS record proof with annual re-verification makes the identity prove its channel on demand: the hardware security key answers a fresh challenge, the DNS record proof is recorded, and annual re-verification keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so a rented or borrowed channel cannot quietly serve ten identities. Like a meadow on a key ring, one odd key hides easily, so the check runs on every binding rather than a sample. From the ledge to the ridge, the same rule holds: no channel, no trust, no exception.
